done_when: An optional test_runner setting in forge.toml picks the machine for the pull-request test jobs only; every other job, including the nightly full test run, uses runner; without test_runner nothing changes

known.title: Doctor diagnoses the wrong runner when PR tests queue

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a separate PR test runner has no available machine and a test remains queued for at least five minutes.
The test job now uses `test_runner`, but `src/forge/checks.py:352` still diagnoses only `runner`. Its scan at lines 365–376 can treat a started `docs-check` job on the ordinary runner as evidence that the test runner is available, suppressing the missing-runner diagnosis; otherwise it names the ordinary runner instead of the unavailable test runner. The client can be directed away from the setting that is blocking CI.
Adds work: make the existing doctor diagnosis use the queued job's runner; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - configuring a separate test runner or upgrading a repo without the setting.
The named proof checks job labels but not event routing: the single-group test job could also run on a nightly or target event and the test would pass. Its Windows check at line 47 looks only for a PowerShell fragment, so it also passes if the command retains that fragment but stops retrying. The existing executable retry test at `tests/test_windows_client_retries.py:33` sets only `runner`, not `test_runner`. Finally, the adopted case compares two workflows generated by the new code after it overwrites the old configuration, so line 49 cannot detect an upgrade changing the previous workflow. The cases labelled new also handwrite a minimal configuration rather than initializing or adopting a client repo. Exercise these behaviors at the generated-workflow boundary and compare the no-override case against an independent pre-change baseline.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_only_pull_request_tests_use_the_optional_machine

why: A client that pays for CI machines pays for every Forge CI job, because one runner setting picks the machine for all of them, including the short jobs and the nightly full test run
